feeOnTop NOT in SWAP_TYPEHASH (by design). limitAmount caps total cost: input swap feeOnTop>amountIn reverts (FeeHelper:53), output swap total checked against limitAmount (AMMModule:2171). No unbounded drain possible.

Reviewed Phase 0 Aderyn artifact (docs/targets/full-system/artifacts/phase0/lbamm-hooks-and-handlers-aderyn.md). CLI aderyn crashes with panic in compile.rs:78. Phase 0 artifact shows: 3 high (centralization risk in setTokenSettings/setTokenFees/setTokenForwardCallHook — known owner-gated design), unused return values in CLOB (informational), state variables that could be constant. Architectural review complete. Diamond proxy at core (slot 0x9A1D), three-tier hook system (Token→Pool→Liquidity), pluggable pool types via ILimitBreakAMMPoolType. Auth boundaries: AMM is sole caller of hook state-changing functions. Registry is sole caller of hook sync. PermitC handles signature verification externally. CLOB uses maker ownership for order management. No cross-boundary auth gaps found — each layer enforces its own access control independently.

H1: feeOnTop manipulation via unsigned field. RULED OUT. Test test_H1_feeOnTop_unsigned_field_manipulation passes. feeOnTop is excluded from SWAP_TYPEHASH but limitAmount (signed) caps total exposure. FeeHelper:53 reverts if feeOnTop > amountIn for input swaps. AMMModule:2171 checks total against limitAmount for output swaps. No profit vector — attacker cannot extract value beyond what signer authorized via limitAmount.

H2: cosigner bypass when cosigner==address(0). RULED OUT. Test test_H2_cosigner_bypass_zero_address passes. When cosigner is address(0), _validateCosignature skips validation — this is intentional design for permits that don't need cosigning. The cosigner field IS signed in the permit, so the signer explicitly chose no cosigner. No auth bypass.

H3: CLOB order nonce manipulation. RULED OUT. Test test_H3_clob_nonce_manipulation passes. nextOrderNonce is auto-incrementing (nextOrderNonce++), stored in contract state, not caller-controlled. Order IDs are sequential and non-reusable. closeOrder checks maker==msg.sender. No way to forge or replay order nonces.

H4: validateHandlerOrder price manipulation without access control. RULED OUT. Test test_H4_validateHandlerOrder_no_access_control passes. Function is view-only (doesn't modify state), called by CLOB's _enforceTokenHooks during settlement. Even if called directly by attacker, it only returns validation result — no state change possible. Pricing bounds enforced when configured.

H5: permit replay across chains/pools. RULED OUT. Test test_H5_permit_replay_cross_chain passes. PermitC uses EIP-712 domain separator with chainId and verifyingContract. Bitmap nonces consumed on use (one-time for fill-or-kill, cumulative for partial-fill). Cross-chain replay impossible due to domain separator. Same-chain replay impossible due to nonce consumption.

H6: hook settings desync between registry and hook cache. RULED OUT. Test test_H6_settings_desync_registry_hook passes. _getOrFetchTokenSettings auto-corrects by fetching from registry when cache is stale. setTokenSettings calls hook.syncTokenSettings to push updates. Even if cache is temporarily stale, next beforeSwap call refreshes it. No exploitable window — at worst, one transaction uses stale settings, then self-heals.

H7: transient storage slot collision between hooks. RULED OUT. Test test_H7_transient_storage_collision passes. Known as HOOK-001/CP-001. DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT is overwritten per-token during beforeSwap (AMM calls beforeSwap for each token). Second write intentionally overwrites first. afterSwap only reads the last-written value. By-design behavior, not exploitable.

H8: CLOB order front-running / sandwich. RULED OUT. Test test_H8_clob_frontrun_sandwich passes. CLOB orders are filled at the maker's specified price (not market price). Attacker cannot manipulate fill price. depositToken/withdrawToken require maker==msg.sender. openOrder price is set by maker. traverseCLOB fills at order prices in linked-list order. No MEV extraction possible beyond normal priority ordering.

H9: partial fill permit amount tracking manipulation. RULED OUT. Test test_H9_partial_fill_amount_tracking passes. PermitC uses cumulative fillable amount tracking — _checkAndUpdateRemainingFillableQuantity ensures total filled never exceeds permitted amount. Bitmap nonce with REUSABLE_COSIGNATURE_NONCE=0 allows reuse but cumulative cap prevents over-extraction. Amount tracking is in PermitC (audited, external to scope).

H10: pool type address validation bypass (6 leading zero bytes requirement). RULED OUT. Test test_H10_pool_type_address_validation passes. AMM validates pool type addresses at pool creation (must have 6 leading zero bytes). This is enforced in lbamm-core, not in hooks-and-handlers. CREATE2 vanity address mining required — not an auth bypass in the handler layer. Pool type registration is admin-only in core.
